stories.title: CRE Continues Holding Up as Occupiers and Investors are More Selective
stories.excerpt: The first half of 2026 generated considerable concern among commercial real estate investors and occupiers. Inflation remained sticky, prompting the Federal Reserve to hold interest rates steady. Tariff and trade uncertainty continued to generate pricing pressures, the Middle East conflict impacted oil prices, and the labor market softened despite a still-low unemployment rate. Yet commercial real estate has continued to perform relatively well. According to a recent CBRE newsletter, occupier demand remains strong, investment activity has increased, and fundamentals continue to improve across property sectors. Several factors are supporting the industry. Limited New Supply Office and retail construction remain near historic lows, while industrial supply growth is leveling off. Apartment starts are also declining. That supply constraint is beginning to affect tenant behavior. Occupiers are planning further ahead to secure early renewals and available space. Meanwhile, increased bank financing is giving owners and investors more opportunities to repurpose obsolete properties into higher-quality assets. Quality Is Changing “Quality” also means something different than it once did. For office occupiers, quality is about attracting and retaining talent rather than newer, shinier finishes. Retailers want space in locations where customers congregate. Industrial tenants look for functionality, including truck-flow efficiency, dock configurations and yard design. While prime office assets continue to attract capital, CBRE said that investors are also looking at well-located, second-generation facilities with existing power that could be converted into data centers. AI Changes the Equation Technology has historically reshaped workplaces and real estate. CBRE said that artificial intelligence will do the same. bullets: Apartment starts declining; office and retail construction near historic lows.
Strong occupier demand, increased bank financing enabling asset repurposing.
Supply constraint driving early renewals and forward tenant planning.
stories.summary: Commercial real estate fundamentals remain resilient despite sticky inflation and rate uncertainty. Apartment starts are declining alongside historically low office and retail construction, creating supply constraints across sectors. Strong occupier demand and improved bank financing availability are enabling owners to repurpose obsolete assets and giving tenants incentive to secure space early.
stories.impact: Declining apartment starts signal a tightening pipeline that will support rent growth in major markets over the next 18–24 months. Developers should accelerate land acquisition and entitlements in high-demand submarkets before supply scarcity fully materializes and competition for sites intensifies.

stories.title: The Real Estate Question About Quantum Computing
stories.excerpt: Quantum computing infrastructure is scaling faster than the real estate needed to support it, according to JLL’s “Future of Quantum Real Estate” report. Today, much of the space and infrastructure is concentrated on university campuses. But over the next decade, JLL said it expects the private sector to play a much larger role. Unlike conventional computers, which use bits to process information, quantum computers use qubits to tackle extraordinarily complex problems. The technology won’t replace conventional computing. Instead, JLL described it as “a high-value layer of compute within the digital infrastructure stack.” That emerging layer will require its own physical infrastructure. It could also generate a new real estate niche. Not Your Average Data Center Quantum real estate refers to the facilities that support the research, fabrication and deployment of quantum computing systems. JLL identified more than 240 quantum facilities across nine asset types and 35 countries. It might be tempting to think of quantum real estate as data center 2.0. But the physical requirements are different. Quantum installations can require a “room within a room,” with dilution refrigerators, vibration isolation and electromagnetic shielding alongside conventional computing equipment. Those systems also rely on low-latency fiber connections to the classical computing infrastructure that includes software, networks and data storage systems. The requirements vary further depending on the type of technology involved. JLL discussed several modalities, including topological, silicon spin, photonic, neutral-atom, trapped-ion, and superconducting systems. Each of these offers different potential applications ranging from cybersecurity and telecommunications to pharmaceuticals, logistics and finance. Universities As the Foundation Higher education institutions currently anchor most quantum ecosystems because they bring together specialized talent, government funding, corporate partnerships
bullets: Quantum computing infrastructure demand scaling faster than available real estate.
Private sector expected to dominate quantum facilities within 10 years; currently concentrated on university campuses.
Quantum real estate requires specialized infrastructure (dilution refrigerators, vibration isolation, shielding) distinct from data center models.
stories.summary: JLL's 'Future of Quantum Real Estate' report identifies over 240 quantum facilities globally across nine asset types. Quantum computing infrastructure demand is outpacing real estate supply, with the private sector poised to become the dominant player over the next decade. Unlike data centers, quantum facilities require specialized environmental controls and isolation systems, creating a distinct real estate niche.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Quantum real estate is a specialized industrial/lab asset class emerging primarily in tech hubs (likely San Francisco, Boston, Austin, Seattle). Indirectly, continued tech sector investment may boost overall employment and housing demand in those metros, but quantum facilities themselves are not a multifamily driver.

stories.title: Madewell to Open Its First Rockefeller Center Store in 2027
stories.excerpt: Tishman Speyer has signed Madewell to a long-term lease for 7,340 square feet at 1 Rockefeller Plaza. Slated to open in 2027, the new store marks Madewell’s first location at Rockefeller Center. Madewell offers premium denim, apparel, and accessories for women and men. Best known for its denim expertise, the brand is recognized for its thoughtful design, innovative approach to denim, and everyday wardrobe essential. The new store will bring the full Madewell experience to life, showcasing the brand’s denim expertise, signature styling, and community-focused programming, according to Tishman Speyer. “Rockefeller Center continues to attract brands that shape culture and consumer behavior globally,” said EB Kelly, senior managing director at Tishman Speyer and head of Rockefeller Center. “Madewell’s decision to establish a presence here reinforces the Center’s unique ability to combine iconic New York identity with modern cultural relevance.” The post Madewell to Open Its First Rockefeller Center Store in 2027 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Madewell signs 7,340 sq ft lease at 1 Rockefeller Plaza, opening 2027.
Tishman Speyer notes Rockefeller Center attracting brands shaping culture globally.
Premium denim retailer expanding flagship presence in premier NYC location.
stories.summary: Madewell has signed a long-term lease for 7,340 square feet at 1 Rockefeller Plaza, marking its first Rockefeller Center location and opening in 2027. The decision reflects broader tenant confidence in flagship retail at iconic Manhattan addresses. Tishman Speyer emphasized the center's ability to combine iconic NYC identity with modern cultural relevance.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Retail lease signings signal consumer spending confidence and tourism strength in Manhattan, which indirectly supports hotel and short-term rental demand but does not meaningfully affect apartment development, supply, or valuations in any specific metro.

stories.title: NAI Capital Lists Owner-User Opportunity in Pasadena’s Playhouse Village District
stories.excerpt: NAI Capital Commercial has listed 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd. in Pasadena’s Playhouse Village District for sale, presenting an owner-user opportunity encompassing approximately 99,280 square feet across eight stories. Executive managing director Ryan Campbell, SIOR, and EVP Scott Martin are representing the property. Built in 1924 and currently vacant, 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd. features a marble-tile lobby, three Otis traction elevators, including two passenger elevators and one freight elevator, and approximately 300 tons of water-cooled chiller capacity. The building also features emergency power supported by two Generac diesel generators and a fully addressable fire alarm and sprinkler system. “530–532 E. Colorado Blvd. represents a rare opportunity for an owner-user to acquire a substantial office building in one of Pasadena’s most walkable and amenity-rich districts,” said campbell. “The combination of scale, parking, transit access and a central Colorado Boulevard location gives an owner the ability to establish a significant long-term presence in Pasadena while taking advantage of a market where owner-user acquisitions have already reduced available office inventory.” The post NAI Capital Lists Owner-User Opportunity in Pasadena’s Playhouse Village District appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NAI Capital lists 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd., 99,280 sq ft, 8-story office, Pasadena.
Built 1924, vacant; owner-user opportunity in walkable Playhouse Village District.
Broker notes owner-user acquisitions reducing available office inventory in Pasadena.
stories.summary: NAI Capital is marketing a rare 8-story, 99,280-square-foot office building at 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd. in Pasadena's Playhouse Village District for owner-user acquisition. The 1924 property, currently vacant, features substantial infrastructure (chiller capacity, generators, modern elevator and fire systems) and prime Colorado Boulevard transit access. The broker notes that owner-user deals have already tightened office inventory in this walkable submarket.
stories.impact: Limited direct impact on multifamily. However, the broker's comment that owner-user acquisitions are reducing Pasadena office inventory may signal corporate demand and employment growth in the area. Developers should monitor whether this translates to population inflow and rental demand growth in Pasadena, particularly for workforce housing near Colorado Boulevard transit corridors.

stories.title: Podcast: How Landlords Can Solve the Tenant Visibility Problem – Sytes’ Rafael Weiss
stories.excerpt: Rafael Weiss is the co-founder of Sytes, a marketplace platform that connects commercial real estate landlords, developers, and brokers with tenants actively looking for space in real time. Rafael came to the problem as a developer who lost a deal because tenant demand was invisible until it was too late, and built Sytes to fix the information asymmetry at the core of retail leasing. The platform serves nearly 350 tenants and over 35,000 active site listings across all 50 states, with clients including Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken, and Dutch Bros. Rafael is based in Boca Raton, Florida. Clients include Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken, Dutch Bros across 50 states.
Platform solves retail leasing information asymmetry and demand visibility gap.
stories.summary: Sytes is a marketplace platform addressing the retail leasing information gap by connecting landlords, developers, and brokers with tenants actively seeking space. The platform serves nearly 350 tenants and 35,000+ active listings across all 50 states, with major REIT and QSR clients. The tool enables real-time demand visibility and earlier deal closure, reducing time and uncertainty in retail leasing.
stories.impact: Indirect relevance to multifamily development. Sytes improves retail leasing efficiency and visibility, which can accelerate retail tenant commitments in mixed-use developments. For multifamily developers planning retail portions of residential projects, better tenant demand data reduces lease-up risk and improves financial underwriting. However, the platform's primary value accrues to retail REITs and developers, not apartment-focused operators.

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Scoops Up More Miami-Dade Affordable Housing
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has bought two more affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County, following two acquisitions last week, bringing the total to $115.4 million and 570 units. The investment firm purchased the remaining piece of the Lafayette housing complex in Miami’s Little River neighborhood for $27 million, property records show. Called Lafayette Plaza, the 201,446-square-foot property houses 136 apartments at 155 Northeast 78th Street. The 14-story asset was completed on a 1.1-acre parcel in 2008. CBRE Capital Markets provided a $18.9 million loan, backed by Freddie Mac. Lafayette Plaza is attached to the 160-unit Lafayette Square building, which Starwood purchased for just under $30 million last week. In the second transaction this week, the Miami Beach-based firm purchased another property in Little River, Emerald Terrace, paying $24.6 million. CBRE Capital Markets once again supplied financing: a $17.2 million, Freddie Mac-backed loan. The complex, built in 2009 facing train tracks, houses 124 apartments and a 24,718-square-foot parking garage at 244 and 290 Northwest 72nd Terrace, near the retail center of the neighborhood, where popular restaurants such as Sunny’s Steakhouse are located. In the fourth acquisition, which closed last week, Starwood purchased the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments for $34 million. The 4.8-acre complex, built in 2011, features 20 three-story buildings near the southern end of the county in the Naranja neighborhood. Mansfield, Mass.-based Gatehouse Group developed and sold the four properties. CBRE’s Tim Flint, Jim Flinn and Jon Romano brokered all the recent sales and financings. A representative for Starwood confirmed the transactions. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management acquires 4 Miami-Dade affordable housing properties for $115.4M, 570 units.
Recent purchases: Lafayette Plaza (136 units, $27M) and Emerald Terrace (124 units, $24.6M) in Little River.
CBRE Capital Markets provided Freddie Mac-backed financing (18.9M and 17.2M loans).
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management has acquired four affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County totaling $115.4 million and 570 units over two weeks. Recent deals include Lafayette Plaza (136 units, $27M) and Emerald Terrace (124 units, $24.6M), both in Little River, with CBRE Capital Markets securing Freddie Mac-backed financing for each. The properties were built in 2008–2009 and benefit from Freddie Mac's affordable housing lending appetite.
stories.impact: Starwood's rapid accumulation of Miami-Dade affordable housing signals strong investor confidence in Freddie Mac-backed portfolios and the asset class's stability. For multifamily developers in Miami-Dade, this highlights institutional capital competition in workforce and affordable segments. Developers should monitor whether Freddie Mac lending availability and credit terms remain favorable, as this is a key financing source for affordable/workforce units. The Little River submarket is seeing institutional consolidation, which may reduce off-market acquisition opportunities.

stories.title: Javits Center Expansion, Tech Upgrades Boosting NYC Hospitality Industry
stories.excerpt: Five years after the Javits Center underwent a $1.5 billion expansion, the Hudson Yards convention venue is continuing to expand its bandwidth to boost its events business and the adjacent New York City hospitality industry. The 3.3 million-square-foot facility recently underwent a $5 million technology upgrade enabling the Javits Center to become the first convention center in the U.S. to provide the newest wireless network, Wi-Fi 7, Commercial Observer can first report. The Wi-Fi 7 system, which debuted last month for Fanatics Fest, provides another competitive edge in attracting more conferences and events going forward, Joyce Leveston, CEO of the Javits Center, told CO. The original Jacob Javits Center opened in 1986. PHOTO: Edmund Vincent Gillon/Museum of the City of New York/Getty Images “So many people who are coming to conventions also want to feel that they can remotely connect with their workplace,” Leveston said on Wednesday, moments before the Javits Center marked its 40th anniversary with a celebration event. “You can’t do that unless you have a state-of-the-art Wi-Fi system.” The technology enhancement is just the latest effort by the Javits Center to up the ante in terms of drawing some of the biggest conferences and events to Manhattan and providing a jolt to New York City’s economy. The Javits Center estimates that its convention bookings generated more than 100,000 hotel stays in the New York City region in 2025. The expansion of the Javits Center, which debuted in May 2021, added 1.2 million square feet to the north side of the complex, including a 55,000-square-foot ballroom and a glass-enclosed sustainable rooftop pavilion touted as the largest green roof in the Northeast. The boost to New York City’s hospitality industry from new investments to the Javits Center is evident across the street at 418 11th Avenue, where a new 455-room Hilton-branded hotel is slated to open in the next three years as part of a larger mixed-use project. The upgrade, which debuted at Fanatics Fest, enhances the facility's ability to attract high-profile conferences and events. This follows a $1.5 billion expansion five years prior and reflects continued investment in NYC's event and hospitality infrastructure.
stories.impact: Strong indirect driver of Manhattan and Hudson Yards multifamily demand. Premium event hosting draws corporate attendees, business travelers, and relocation candidates to NYC, boosting hotel occupancy and indirect demand for furnished rentals and corporate housing. Developers should view Javits Center investment as a signal of sustained NYC tourism and business travel strength, supporting both core Manhattan and nearby Hudson Yards residential development pipelines.

stories.title: Westphal Company Lands $56M Refi for San Diego Apartments
stories.excerpt: The Westphal Company has secured $56.1 million in permanent financing for a 354-unit apartment complex in eastern San Diego County. Northmarq arranged the fixed-rate financing through the firm’s Fannie Mae platform. The nonrecourse loan carries a 10-year term with interest-only payments for the full term. Property records identify Westphal Company owns the Wintercrest Village Apartments, a garden-style community at 12002 Wintercrest Drive in Lakeside, Calif., which is an unincorporated community roughly 20 miles northeast of Downtown San Diego. The property features one- and two-bedroom apartments, along with two swimming pools and spas, outdoor courtyards, and fitness rooms. Northmarq’s Aaron Beck, Conor Freeman and Robbie Driscoll facilitated the financing, which allowed Westphal to extract equity from the property while maintaining its cash flow, according to Beck. The lender also waived all operating escrows. “With this Fannie Mae refinance, we were able to unlock trapped equity for the borrower and preserve cash flow while keeping the loan truly non-recourse with no carve-out guarantees,” Beck said in a statement. San Diego’s multifamily market stabilized in the second quarter, with vacancy holding at 5 percent and asking rents rising 0.5 percent to $2,598 per month, according to Northmarq’s second-quarter data. Investment sales slowed roughly 25 percent compared to last year, but median pricing jumped 25 percent to $415,000 per unit. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Westphal Company secures $56.1M refi for 354-unit Wintercrest Village Apartments, Lakeside, San Diego.
Fannie Mae fixed-rate, 10-year, interest-only loan; nonrecourse; operating escrows waived.
Loan extracts equity while preserving cash flow; property 20 miles northeast of Downtown San Diego.
stories.summary: The Westphal Company has refinanced Wintercrest Village Apartments, a 354-unit garden-style community in Lakeside (San Diego County), with $56.1 million in permanent Fannie Mae financing. The 10-year fixed-rate loan includes interest-only payments, nonrecourse terms, and waived operating escrows, enabling equity extraction while maintaining cash flow. The property is located approximately 20 miles northeast of Downtown San Diego.
stories.impact: Demonstrates continued Fannie Mae appetite for garden-style multifamily refinancing and equity extraction, signaling stable debt markets for established, stabilized properties. San Diego's outer-ring submarkets (like Lakeside) continue to attract institutional capital and favorable financing, reflecting sustained demand and lower development risk. Developers should note that Fannie Mae's willingness to waive escrows and offer favorable terms on proven assets may create opportunities for land acquisition in adjacent San Diego submarkets where rental demand and property quality justify new construction.

stories.title: Fortress Refinances Dania Design Center With $45M After Foreclosure Fight
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has refinanced the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach, Fla., following a nasty foreclosure fight with its previous owner, New York-based billionaire Charles Cohen. City National Bank of Florida supplied a $45 million loan backing the 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex at 1855 Griffin Road, facing the I-95. In the past two years, Fortress has invested about $3 million updating the campus, which dates back to 1988. Another $3 million to $5 million of renovations are planned over the coming year. In June, it tapped Jamestown to oversee management and leasing of the mixed-use property. The move comes about five years after the Design Center lost one of its main tenants, online pet retailer Chewy, which occupied about 100,000 square feet, when it relocated to Plantation Pointe. Fortress won control of Design Center and the neighboring Le Méridien Dania Beach hotel in 2024, through a $76 million credit bid. The proceeding was part of a broader foreclosure suit with Cohen Realty Enterprises, which Charles Cohen’s father Sherman Cohen had founded in the 1950s. In 2022, the New York-based lender provided a $535 million debt package, covering several commercial properties, including Cohens’s Dania Beach assets. The billionaire also personally guaranteed a $187 million portion of the loan. A year later, Cohen defaulted, prompting Fortress to take control of the commercial real estate. The lender also went after the borrower’s personal assets, believing the commercial properties were worth less than what Cohen owed, the Wall Street Journal reported. These include a chateau and vineyard estate in the south of France, a 220-foot megayacht, and a collection of Ferraris. In response, Cohen sold off several properties in New York. In June, Cohen announced that he had paid off the full judgement. But the legal battle remains, with Cohen filing to recoup $204 million in alleged damages. bullets: Fortress Investment Group refinances Design Center of Americas, Dania Beach, for $45M post-foreclosure.

stories.summary: Fortress Investment Group has refinanced the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach with a $45 million loan from City National Bank of Florida following a foreclosure battle with previous owner Charles Cohen. The 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex has received $3 million in upgrades with another $3–5 million planned. Fortress acquired control via $76 million credit bid in 2024 and engaged Jamestown for management and leasing.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. However, Fortress's stabilization of a distressed office asset signals that institutional capital is willing to resolve troubled CRE and reposition it for long-term hold, reducing risk of market dumping. For South Florida multifamily developers, the refocus on Design Center (near I-95 in Dania Beach) indicates that office repositioning and employment concentration may support adjacent residential development. Monitor whether Fortress's leasing efforts and capital reinvestment in Dania Beach signal broader commercial recovery in the corridor.
